nodes.subject: clean-label concept
nodes.object: clean labels omit perceived undesirable ingredients and may display natural claims but need not be additive-free and have no exact universal definition

support_spans.exact_quote: A clean label is a label on a food, not listing ingredients that may be perceived by consumers as undesirable.
It does not necessarily mean that the product is free from additives
There is no exact definition of which ingredients precisely may be included or excluded in a clean label.

accepted_phrases: The clean-label page describes omitting ingredients perceived as undesirable and displaying natural or no-artificial claims, but says this need not mean additive-free and has no exact included-or-excluded ingredient definition. It is general marketing and formulation context, not an audit or a health or safety result for an exact offer.

nodes.subject: monosodium glutamate
nodes.object: MSG is the sodium salt of glutamic acid and can enhance savory or umami perception

support_spans.exact_quote: Monosodium glutamate ( MSG ), also known as sodium glutamate ,  is a sodium salt of glutamic acid .
MSG is used in cooking as a flavor enhancer with a savory taste that intensifies the umami flavor of food
MSG balances, blends, and rounds the perception of other tastes.

accepted_phrases: The MSG page identifies monosodium glutamate as the sodium salt of glutamic acid and describes a savory or umami flavor-enhancing function. These are identity and flavor-mechanism facts only; they do not establish an exact snack formula, amount, exposure, child-specific outcome, medical conclusion or product safety ranking.

Only the glutamate ion is responsible for the umami flavor, so the effect does not depend significantly on the starting compound.

many additives having both natural and artificial origin were introduced.
